name: Sulfur recovery (Claus, tail gas treating, SuperClaus)
applications: LNG plants with H2S in feed
principle: Acid gas is partly burned in a reaction furnace, converting 60 to 70% of the H2S, and the rest reacts with SO2 over catalytic converters to make elemental sulfur, taking recovery beyond 95% (BASF). A tail gas unit hydrogenates the remaining sulfur species to H2S over a CoMo catalyst and removes it with a selective amine, which BASF and Baker Hughes say lifts total recovery above 99.9%.

performance.metric: H2S conversion in the reaction furnace

source.note: BASF SRU tail gas treatment brochure, 2020

performance.metric: overall sulfur recovery with hydrogenation/amine tail gas treating

source.note: BASF SRU tail gas treatment brochure, 2020

advantages: High recovery with tail gas treating
limitations: Tail gas treating adds cost and complexity
Sensitive to ammonia, hydrocarbons and BTEX in acid gas
Sulfur markets can be weak far from buyers

sources.note: BASF SRU tail gas treatment brochure, 2020
